title: An ample inversion norm detects positivity of a cubical line
statement: Let $S$ be a normal integral Noetherian affine scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-integral-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth, def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]; Noetherian means locally Noetherian and quasi-compact, and normal means that all local rings are integrally closed domains. Let $p:G\to S$ be a smooth separated commutative group scheme of finite presentation [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation, def-sc-group-scheme] with semiabelian geometric fibres [def-sfb-semiabelian-geometric-fibres]. Its multiplication $m:G\times_SG\to G$, identity $e:S\to G$, and inversion $\iota:G\to G$ are $S$-morphisms satisfying associativity, identity, inverse and commutativity identities [def-pc-fibre-product]. Separated means that its diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Let $(P,r,\tau)$ be a cubical rigidified invertible module on $G$ [def-sfb-cubical-rigidified-line, def-sc-invertible-module]. Use tensor pullback and tensor product [def-pc-module-pullback, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Suppose the specified line $N=P\otimes\iota^*P$ is ample on the WHOLE scheme $G$ [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. Then $P$ is ample on $G$. The hypothesis is absolute ampleness of this supplied global inversion norm, not ampleness of its residue-field restrictions; no conclusion about extending a line from a generic fibre is asserted.

source.place: Agent-formulated norm-reflection input to the cubical ampleness argument; the normal-base relative version is a separate unsplit theorem, not claimed as a numbered assertion of Raynaud. Original ampleness chapters WANTED.

proof.text: Set $D=P\otimes(\iota^*P)^\vee$. Apply [lem-sfb-cubical-antisymmetric-frame-extension] to the given cubical rigidified $P$. Obtain the actual frame scheme $q:E=D^\times\to G$ with its commutative group law. In particular $E/S$ is smooth separated of finite presentation with semiabelian geometric fibres; $q$ is affine, faithfully flat of finite presentation and a group quotient with kernel $\mathbf G_{m,S}$. Its tautological frame trivializes $q^*D$. The given normal integral Noetherian affine base is unchanged.

source.place: I, cubical torsors and associated extensions (especially the cube/second-difference calculus in I 2 and I 5). Agent-formulated antisymmetric-frame construction; local original WANTED, not a claimed verbatim numbered theorem. The multiplication is obtained from the cube at (x,y,-x-y).

proof.text: Let $N=P\otimes\iota^*P$, the supplied ample line. Rank-one evaluation and tensor symmetry identify $P^{\otimes2}\simeq N\otimes D$: the factors $\iota^*P$ and $(\iota^*P)^\vee$ cancel. Pullback distributes over tensor products by [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor]. Using $q^*D\simeq\mathcal O_E$ from step 1 gives $q^*(P^{\otimes2})\simeq q^*N$. These are isomorphisms of invertible modules on the whole schemes; no fibrewise comparison is used. Evaluation is checked in any local frame, where it is $a\otimes b\mapsto ab$, and these maps agree on overlaps.

source.place: Tensor-pullback and rank-one evaluation, explicit local-frame cancellation.

proof.text: Since $q$ is affine and $N$ is ample on all of $G$, [lem-weil-pbc-pullback-ample-invertible] makes $q^*N$ ample on all of $E$. Transport its sections through the preceding line isomorphism: their residue values and nonvanishing loci agree, so $q^*(P^{\otimes2})$ is ample.

source.place: Affine pullback of an ample invertible module, as stated in the cited node; transport along an isomorphism.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-semiabelian-gm-extension-ample-reflection] to $q:E\to G$ and $M=P^{\otimes2}$. Step 1 supplies its full group-extension, smoothness, separation, finite-presentation and semiabelian-fibre hypotheses; the base meets exactly its normal integral Noetherian affine assumptions. Step 3 supplies absolute ampleness upstairs. Therefore $P^{\otimes2}$ is ample on $G$.

source.place: XI 1.11, ampleness comparison for group quotients: supporting source for the field abelian-quotient case. The relative semiabelian Gm-extension assertion here is an agent-formulated geometric prerequisite, not claimed as the verbatim statement of XI 1.11. Original and proof of this relative formulation WANTED. No general fpqc descent of absolute ampleness is asserted.

proof.text: By [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module], $G$ is quasi-compact and every $x\in G$ has an affine section locus $G_s$ containing $x$ for some $s\in\Gamma(G,(P^{\otimes2})^{\otimes n})$, $n\geq1$. Regard $s$ as a section of $P^{\otimes2n}$ by reassociating tensor factors. Its residue value and locus are unchanged and $2n\geq1$. The same affine loci and quasi-compactness verify the definition for $P$, proving the conclusion.

source.place: Tag 01PS, definition of ampleness; positive-power reflection directly from the affine section loci.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NV-09faedb90 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole split. The item statement and stmt_deps are unchanged from live, the item is still unsplit on live and side-live (so no parallel group superseded it), there is no repair note, and no SGA source is used. Step 1 cites the new lem-sfb-cubical-antisymmetric-frame-extension with H=G and L=P; its hypotheses are exactly the item's. I checked by hand that the cube identity at (x,y,-x-y) gives D_xD_y ≅ D_{x+y}. Commutativity follows from the S_3 symmetry of tau. The associativity and commutativity defects are normalized units, which Rosenlicht's theorem forces to be trivial. Each fibre of E is an extension of a torus by G_m over a semiabelian fibre, so it is semiabelian. Step 2 is the identity P^{⊗2} ≅ N⊗D, which is elementary, plus pullback of tensor products (lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor (2)), giving q*P^2 ≅ q*N. Step 3 uses that q is affine and N is ample, so q*N is ample (Stacks 0892(2), morphisms.tex l.8829). Step 4 applies the new lem-sfb-semiabelian-gm-extension-ample-reflection; every hypothesis is supplied by step 1, and the kernel is G_m by fppf exactness. Step 5 passes from P^2 to P using the same affine loci with exponent 2n (Stacks 01PS, properties.tex l.4244). I tested the reflection node on: a trivial extension (restrict to H×{1}); H a torus; a field with D non-torsion (then E is not quasi-affine); H an abelian scheme (fibres plus the field case); a DVR with generic elliptic fibre and special fibre G_m (Pic(H)=Pic(H_eta)); and E quasi-affine (then H is a torus). A general G_m-torsor counterexample such as A^{n+1}∖0 → P^n is excluded by the group hypothesis. The node is not a duplicate of the field-only abelian-quotient-ample-reflection, of subtorus-quotient-schematicity, of fpqc descent or of algebraic-equivalence-norm. The frame node is not a duplicate of picard-multiplicative-torsor, second-difference-diagonal or def-sfb-cubical-rigidified-line. Both new nodes are honestly labelled as agent-formulated, with the Raynaud XI 1.11 and Moret-Bailly I originals marked WANTED. The generic sec-proper-base-change tool uses are accepted. FIX (B2): the frame-extension statement never declared H to be a commutative S-group scheme and used m, e, p_1 and p_2 without introducing them. The corrected statement is in fixes/dag/nodes/sec-six-functors-basics/lem-sfb-cubical-antisymmetric-frame-extension.json.; 1 file(s) fixed by the reviewer
